Once upon a time, in a bustling city with glimmering lights and shadows of hardship, lived a slim girl named Lila. Lila came from a family that had struggled to make ends meet her whole life. Despite their trials, her family loved one another deeply, but Lila harbored a dream that none of them could quite understand: she wanted to be fat.

To Lila, being fat represented abundance. It meant never feeling the chilling pangs of hunger again, never being the subject of pitying glances at her threadbare clothes. By society's standards, Lila was conventionally attractive—her slim figure and delicate features drew admiration—but she despised the fragility that poverty and malnutrition had etched into her body. She wanted to know what it felt like to overflow, to take up space, to feel permanent and undeniable in the world.

One day, after searching for opportunities, she wandered into a cozy yet aging restaurant on a side street. The sign above read, *"Martha's Homestyle Kitchen,"* though the peeling paint and cracked windows hinted at its struggles. Lila saw an opportunity. She approached the owner, a gruff middle-aged man named Greg, and made him a shocking offer.

“I’ll work as a waitress,” she said boldly, “but you don’t have to pay me. All I need is a place to stay and the leftover food each night. That’s all.”

Greg squinted at her, dubious. “Why would anyone work for no money? What’s the catch?”

“No catch. Just think of it as me helping you save costs. You get a worker, I get food and a roof over my head. Deal?”

Greg, desperate to cut corners in his failing restaurant, reluctantly agreed. He didn’t think much of her strange request for leftovers, but he also didn’t expect her to last long. After all, most staff barely stuck around due to the restaurant's poor reputation for food quality. Customers rarely returned, and plates often went back to the kitchen untouched or half-eaten. For Lila, this was a gold mine.

And so, Lila started her new life. Day after day, she worked tirelessly, serving the sparse but unhappy customers and earning glares when food returned to the kitchen. At night, she would retreat to a small, dusty storage room Greg let her use, where she devoured the uneaten portions with fervor. No morsel went to waste—half a steak, soggy fries, cold soup—she consumed everything, relishing the feeling of fullness she had long craved.

Initially, the changes in her body were subtle. Her cheeks filled out, her arms gained some softness. She smiled when she looked into the cracked mirror in the storage room. Finally, she was on her way to becoming the person she always dreamed of—a symbol of abundance and comfort.

However, Lila’s obsession grew unbridled. The restaurant’s poor food quality didn’t matter as long as it was plentiful. She even started sneaking out of the bin outside to scrape together every crumb Greg threw out. Over months, she gained more and more weight, her once-light frame expanding rapidly in the solitude of her tiny room.

But as her body grew heavier, her world began to shrink.

One morning, after a fitful night of overeating, Lila realized with alarm that she could no longer squeeze through the narrow bathroom door attached to the main dining area. At first, she treated it as a minor inconvenience—she could manage without it. But as the days passed and her size continued to balloon, other issues began to stack up. She couldn’t fit through the front door, which meant she could no longer leave the restaurant. Her hygiene deteriorated as she had no access to proper facilities. The once-cozy storage room became a prison, filled with sour smells and shadows of regret.

Customers began to notice. They complained about the overpowering odor that seemed to seep into the dining area from the back. Word spread about Martha’s Homestyle Kitchen, but not in the way Greg had hoped. Rumors of unsanitary conditions and poor management drove away what little business the restaurant had left. Unable to cover his costs, Greg declared bankruptcy and abandoned the restaurant altogether, leaving Lila behind in her self-made cocoon.

Now, Lila was utterly alone. She could no longer work, could no longer fit through any door, and the food she once saw as her salvation had rotted alongside her dreams. The abandoned restaurant fell into disrepair: cobwebs overtook the corners, dust blanketed the countertops, and mold crept across the walls. Animals and insects scavenged alongside her, whispering reminders of her isolation. The very body she once longed for now chained her to the ruins of her own choices.

As days turned to weeks, and weeks to months, Lila sat in the darkened remains of the restaurant, surrounded by silence and memories of clinking plates and muffled laughter. She realized too late that her desire to overindulge, to grow beyond her beginnings, had consumed more than food—it had consumed her ability to truly live.

By the time anyone thought to look for what had become of the failed restaurant, it was far too late to save her, leaving only whispers of her story for those who would listen.

And so, Lila’s hunger for abundance became her cautionary tale—a tale of unchecked desires and dreams pursued without care for the consequences.
